en.title: ee
en.summary: This is the letter L318 from the vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: Sound of the letters
paragraphs: The letters ee sound like the long vowel /iː/. Their standard sound is the sound in (tree) /triː/, which means a tall plant with wood and leaves. These two letters have two sounds in total. Most words use the long sound, but some common words use a shorter sound instead.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, spread your lips wide into a smile. Raise the front of your tongue close to the top of your mouth. For the second sound, relax your tongue slightly down and toward the center. Keep your lips relaxed rather than spread wide. Feel your vocal cords vibrate with your hand on your throat for both sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In most regular words, these letters produce the long sound /iː/, as in (see) /siː/. They also make that same sound in the middle of a word, as in (feed) /fiːd/. In a few special words, these letters produce the shorter sound /ɪ/, as in (been) /bɪn/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make the long sound too short, like the vowel in sit. Remember to spread your lips into a clear smile and stretch the sound. When you say the shorter vowel, do not tense your mouth into a full smile. Relax your lips and tongue so the vowel does not sound like seat.
